notes.note: Reviewed home schema and rollback claims against the registry addition: the principal feed is state and does not alter channel isolation or schema policy.
Reviewed the historical browser subscription finding against the revised Web Push guide and resolver: principal feeds do not change browser subscriptions or produce push.
Reviewed scheduler composition and native notification feed claims against runtime support: membership is passed into NotificationService; scheduler wiring and the decided OS feed are unchanged.
Reviewed readiness and evidence ownership against runtime support: injecting Project membership into notifications does not change governance evidence or gate semantics.
Reviewed notification provider, scheduling and delivery distinctions against runtime support and the private feed: provider actions and OS delivery remain separate.

Reviewed the scheduler and notification foundations in this retained proposal against runtime support: membership injection does not alter automation intake, scheduler dispatch or the proposal status.
Reviewed the dispatch composition and task lifecycle claims against runtime support: notification membership injection does not change Task dispatch, cancellation or recovery.
Reviewed backup and rollback claims against the registry: media tools remain external, and the separate principal notification file is classified as product state.

Reviewed resolver, runtime composition and private feed against the service and focused tests: membership is checked before the synchronous write; no principal delivery event or push is emitted; route and preferences remain future work.
Reviewed the home backup and rollback description against the registry: the new principal notification file is state and does not change CLI commands or external exclusions.
Reviewed notification hooks and owner notification API against the changed contract and service: existing APIs keep their owner behavior; no principal feed SDK route is claimed.

Updated and reviewed the envelope write contract against the parser and service: principal writes require a human ID and Project ID, legacy reads remain compatible, and membership admission is separate from shape validation.
